work.text: A Mongol conqueror riding a white horse gazes stonily at his defeated West Asian opponent in a scene that took place more than 300 years before this painting was made.

work.text: Visually, the diagonal composition with cityscape at the top of the page—also found among the earliest Mughal paintings—was expanded to include throngs of participants and a startling new naturalism.

moment.text: Identified pages from this [Akbar-period] copy relate to the second half of the first section, the history of Genghis Khan, specifically known as the Kitab-i-Chingiz-nama (Book of the History of Genghis), and Abu’l Fazl mentions it under this name in the A’in-i-Akbari.

source.author: Milo Cleveland Beach
source.title: The Imperial Image: Paintings for the Mughal Court

moment.text: Painting from the Akbar period reached its maturity by the 1590s in works such as this: dynamic in composition and gestures but contained within organized spaces and emphasized three-dimensionality.
